teaser: The officer put an adult's wording back into the green journal for one morning, and the plant never read a word of it: what it wanted was the crown lamps lit, and a seven-year-old found that out by holding a hand lamp against the wall. The farm gave the light, the flower opened wide — and then the count ran out on the man who wrote the line, so the new rule now has a tooth behind it. Hesper has a flower that will ask for a name and no dead child to give it, and only one name on the farm that nobody is allowed to say again.
